quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and look carefully before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look carefully before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be careful. Slow down and look both ways before you drive through the intersection.

questions.question: As it gets darker, what lights should you turn on so others can see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beam headlights when daylight begins to fade. Use high beams only when driving in open areas with no other cars nearby.

questions.question: What should you do when you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Stop and wait until they have completely crossed.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until they have completely crossed.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind. You must stop and let them cross completely before you drive. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
The road splits. You must go either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road splits. You must go either right or left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that the road divides ahead. You must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: You are driving behind a large truck on the freeway. How far back should you drive?

options.text: Closer than you would follow a regular car.
Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and prepare to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
questions.explanation: Drive farther behind a large truck because trucks have bigger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: You want to turn right. A pedestrian with a guide dog is at the corner ready to cross. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine while they cross.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait for them to cross first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for them to cross first.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times. Always let them cross before you turn.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Cut across traffic quickly to make the exit.
Make a U-turn to go back to your exit.
Continue driving and take the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and take the next exit.
questions.explanation: Never cut across traffic or make sudden turns to reach an exit. Keep driving safely and use the next exit instead.

questions.question: On a multilane highway, a car is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match their speed.
Move right and let them pass.
Slow down to annoy the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right and let them pass.
questions.explanation: On multilane roads, move to the right lane and let the tailgating driver pass. The left lane is for faster-moving traffic.

questions.question: When you pass another car, how should you do it?

options.text: Pass slowly.
Drive at the same speed as the other car.
Pass quickly and safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass quickly and safely.
questions.explanation: Pass as quickly and safely as possible to complete the pass fast. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror.

questions.question: What turn is this bicyclist signaling?

options.text: A left turn.
A stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicycles use hand signals instead of turn signals. When a bicyclist extends their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: You should drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, driving too slowly and blocking normal traffic flow is illegal and may result in a citation.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigued driving dangers, take breaks every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may be merging into your lane ahead.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Sound your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, your right, then your left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, your right, then your left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer. Check across the entire intersection before moving.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt system. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle the lap belt.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and put on hazard lights.
Put on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, get it off the road and away from traffic if possible. Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. To prevent hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down in rainy weather to reduce hydroplaning risk. Driving too fast causes tires to ride on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently and gradually so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Wait for time to pass.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Alcohol stays in your system for a long time. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise will not lower your blood alcohol level. Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal before changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal to warn other drivers. Check your mirrors and turn your head to see your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: It is illegal to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone.
Pass over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see ahead clearly. Do not pass at crossings, railroad crossings, or where no passing signs are posted. Do not pass when a solid yellow line is on your side of the road.

questions.question: At a crosswalk:

options.text: You must let pedestrians go first.
Pedestrians must let you go first.
Construction workers have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings if they follow traffic signals. Vehicles must stop for pedestrians in marked or unmarked crosswalks.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?

options.text: Only look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and left shoulder for left lane changes.
Two outside mirrors mean there are no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right lane changes and left shoulder for left lane changes.
questions.explanation: Signal first, check mirrors, then look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side means:

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass. Both solid yellow lines mean no one can pass safely in either direction.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal. Drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep the same speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the same speed.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not speed up or brake hard. Keep a steady speed and let the other vehicle safely return to your lane.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always be very careful when backing up.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road intersects ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road intersects ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to things they may not see right away. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that a side road will cross ahead.

questions.question: Temporary signs used in construction and maintenance work areas:

options.text: Have a red background with green writing.
Have an orange background with black writing.
Have a yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Create a habit when getting in and out of your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Challenge them.
Get out of their way.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of their way.
questions.explanation: Drivers must respect other road users and follow the rules to prevent crashes. When you see an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to get out of their way. Never try to compete with other drivers.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to let any vehicle or pedestrian already in the intersection pass. You may go slowly if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area set aside for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are often marked with white lines to show where pedestrians should cross. Some crosswalks have extra lines between or instead of the parallel lines. Some crosswalks have no markings at all.

questions.question: You are required to stop your vehicle:

options.text: At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
Where there is a red traffic light.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely at a steady or flashing red traffic light. You must always obey police officers directing traffic, no matter what signs or traffic signals say.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the accelerator or brake to help the vehicle regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to get control back.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle, look in your rearview mirror for both headlights of the car you passed. Only then is it safe to move back to your original lane.
